scope: Offline saved-metadata analysis and new preparation-only callable. No CLI launch, validation helper dispatch, producer integration or execution approval.

journal.format: append-only JSONL, exclusive-create, synchronous bounded writes; no paths, package names, raw exception text or inputs
journal.clock: monotonic; never resets or extends original preflight deadline
journal.last_item_index: zero-based completed loop item; distribution rows only hashed/enumerated until final aggregate reference hash matches
journal.bytes: actual bytes fed to completed SHA256 reads, including input inventory control. Partial failed hash reads are unavailable and not included, rather than estimated.
journal.write_frequency: one bounded record per completed item and each stage boundary; no event sampling; telemetry adds runtime and I/O overhead
journal.flush: unbuffered writes per event; fsync at normal/error finalization; disk failure invalidates telemetry
journal.on_exception: record current interrupted stage and completed item progress; preserve original exception type and identity check result
journal.on_SIGKILL: at most a prefix persists, last durable item may lag. No summary means incomplete evidence.
journal.final_summary: exclusive-create; identity_check_passed and telemetry_valid are separate; both required for preparation_only_pass. No acceptance proof or authorization.

identity_semantics.record_order: existing distribution iterator order before aggregate sort, existing manifest/inventory dictionary iteration order; no new ordering
identity_semantics.hash_passes: one per original occurrence; count byte lengths during same reads, not second file scan
identity_semantics.loop_item_vs_stage: An item can complete before a later aggregate check fails. Stage completion requires all original stage checks.

fault_policy: Telemetry write/open/flush/close/size failure does not alter identity checking; it makes diagnostic evidence invalid, which is HOLD. Identity failures are not replaced by telemetry failures.
supervision_limits: Original setup check() remains cooperative at original positions, so a blocking read may delay detecting deadline; no new hard realtime guarantee.
Storage stage and source checks still run in original order; telemetry only records already reached work.
New preparation wrapper does not dispatch B/C, allocate a new trial allowance, or revive old authorization.
Before any target use: independent review, new fully bound launch identity and separate once-only authorization; old manifests/output roots remain closed.
